beats.lead: The most mocked font on earth
beats.text: was drawn for a cartoon dog.
beats.note: Comic Sans exists because of Rover, the animated dog in Microsoft Bob, a mid-90s program meant to make the PC friendly for beginners.

beats.name: Vincent Connare
beats.role: A Microsoft designer. He opened a beta of Bob and found the dog speaking through a Times New Roman speech bubble. 'Dogs don't talk in Times New Roman,' he said, and started drawing.

beats.note: Connare modelled the letters on the hand-lettering in graphic novels sitting on his desk, a casual voice for a cartoon, never meant for résumés or wedding invitations.
Comic Sans wasn't finished in time to ship inside Microsoft Bob. It went out later with Windows 95 instead, and from there leaked onto every desktop on the planet.

beats.text: The font built for the dog never made it into the dog's program.

beats.line: From a cartoon dog to CERN's Higgs boson slide.
